{
  "research_question": "Does stimulation paradigm (Combined, ICMS Only, Dim Visual Only, Bright Visual Only, Sham) significantly affect mouse navigation performance metrics (Time-to-Target, Success, Path Efficiency, Average Speed, AD)?",
  "stim_paradigms_compared": ["Combined", "ICMS Only", "Dim Visual Only", "Bright Visual Only", "Sham"],
  "response_variables": ["Time-to-Target", "Success", "Path Efficiency", "Average Speed", "AD"],
  "anova_plan": [
    "Perform a one-way ANOVA for each of the five response variables with 'Stim Paradigm' as the fixed factor.",
    "For 'Success' (binary 0/1), acknowledge that ANOVA is technically applicable but less powerful than logistic regression; proceed with ANOVA for consistency but flag for potential Type I error inflation due to non-normality.",
    "For 'Path Efficiency', check for extreme skewness given the wide range (0.0009 to 29.8); if normality fails, consider a log-transformation or non-parametric Kruskal-Wallis test.",
    "For 'Time-to-Target', check for outliers given the max value (201.39) vs mean (2.80); consider robust ANOVA or log-transformation if residuals are heavily skewed.",
    "For 'Average Speed' and 'AD', proceed with standard ANOVA if residuals approximate normality and variances are homogeneous."
  ],
  "assumptions_and_diagnostics": [
    "Independence of observations: Verify that each row represents a unique trial from a distinct mouse or that clustering by Mouse is accounted for (current summary does not show random effects structure).",
    "Normality of residuals: Inspect Q-Q plots and histograms of residuals for each paradigm group for all five response variables.",
    "Homogeneity of variances: Conduct Levene's test or Bartlett's test across the five stimulation paradigms for each response variable.",
    "Outlier detection: Identify extreme values in 'Time-to-Target' and 'Path Efficiency' that may violate normality assumptions.",
    "Sample size balance: Note the unbalanced design (Combined n=48846 vs Sham n=3505) and assess its impact on power and Type I error rates."
  ],
  "posthoc_plan": [
    "If the omnibus F-test is significant for any variable, conduct pairwise comparisons using Tukey's HSD to control family-wise error rate.",
    "For 'Success', if ANOVA is used, interpret mean differences as differences in proportions; alternatively, report Chi-square tests of independence for each pair.",
    "If normality assumptions are violated for 'Path Efficiency' or 'Time-to-Target', switch to Dunn's test with Bonferroni correction following a Kruskal-Wallis test.",
    "Report effect sizes (eta-squared or Cohen's d) for significant pairwise differences to quantify the magnitude of paradigm effects."
  ],
  "expected_findings": [
    "Combined stimulation likely yields superior performance (lower Time-to-Target, higher Success, higher Path Efficiency, higher Average Speed) compared to Sham or single-modality conditions.",
    "ICMS Only and Dim Visual Only may show intermediate performance, potentially differing from Bright Visual Only depending on the specific sensory integration required for the task.",
    "AD (angular dispersion) is expected to be lowest in Combined and highest in Sham, indicating better directional control with multimodal stimulation.",
    "Significant main effects are anticipated for all five response variables given the large sample size (n=76655) and the distinct theoretical mechanisms of the paradigms."
  ],
  "limitations": [
    "The dataset is heavily unbalanced (Combined has ~64% of data), which may bias variance estimates and reduce power for detecting differences in smaller groups like Sham.",
    "Potential pseudoreplication: If multiple trials per mouse are averaged without modeling the 'Mouse' as a random effect, standard errors may be underestimated.",
    "Skewness in 'Time-to-Target' and 'Path Efficiency' may violate ANOVA assumptions, requiring transformation or non-parametric alternatives.",
    "Binary nature of 'Success' makes ANOVA suboptimal compared to logistic regression, potentially inflating Type I error rates.",
    "No information on temporal autocorrelation or learning effects across trials is available in the summary."
  ],
  "recommended_next_analysis": "Fit a linear mixed-effects model (LMM) for each response variable with 'Stim Paradigm' as a fixed effect and 'Mouse' as a random intercept to account for repeated measures, followed by likelihood ratio tests and post-hoc pairwise comparisons with p-value adjustment."
}
